| File | For |
|---|---|
| `TurboDL-Setup-0.6.0.exe` | Windows 10/11 (x64) |
| `TurboDL-0.6.0-arm64.dmg` | macOS on Apple Silicon (M1 and newer) |
| `TurboDL-0.6.0-x64.dmg` | macOS on Intel |

## What's new

- **The `turbodl` command.** Download from a terminal with everything TurboDL can do: files, X and YouTube videos, HLS/DASH streams, Instagram posts, reels, stories, highlights, profiles and Saved collections. `turbodl get <link>` waits and prints the saved files' paths; `add`, `wait`, `list`, `status` and `cancel` work with queued jobs; `--json` prints one JSON object per line for scripts, and the exit code says how it went. Open **Settings → Command line → Install command line tool** to put it on your PATH, then open a new terminal and run `turbodl --help`. TurboDL starts by itself in the background when it is closed.
- **Python.** `turbodl-client` lets Python scripts do the same: `TurboDL().get(link)` returns the job with its files, and errors come as exceptions. Install it with `pip install "git+https://github.com/AlperKutay/TurboDL#subdirectory=clients/python"` (Python 3.9 or newer).
- **A local API for other programs.** While TurboDL runs it listens on `127.0.0.1` for jobs, protected by a token in `api.json` in its user data folder. The README describes it.
- **Public Instagram profiles without signing in.** A profile opened signed out shows what Instagram shows visitors: its first posts and its highlights. Pick posts to download them; backing up a profile and opening highlights still need a sign-in.
- **A folder per account.** A new setting, on by default, puts Instagram downloads in `Instagram/<account>/` and highlights in `Instagram/<account>/Highlights/`. Turn it off in **Settings → Instagram** to keep the earlier layout.
- Instagram jobs from the command or the API go through the same pacing as the app's screens: one page at a time, with a pause between them, and nothing while Instagram asks TurboDL to slow down.

## Updating

- Install the new version over the old one and open TurboDL once.
- With the per-account setting on, highlights go to `Instagram/<account>/Highlights/`. Stories you backed up before stay in `Instagram/<account> · Highlights` and are not downloaded again; later backups put only new stories in the new folder. Move the old folder's files into the new one if you want them together, or turn the setting off.
- The browser extension has not changed; there is nothing to reload.
- Firefox: open `TurboDL-Firefox-0.6.0.xpi` in Firefox. Regular Firefox only installs add-ons signed by Mozilla; if this file is unsigned, use Firefox Developer Edition, Nightly or ESR with `xpinstall.signatures.required` set to `false`.

The Windows installer is not signed yet: choose **More info → Run anyway**. Windows may also ask about `turbodl.exe` the first time you run the command.
